transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A 'funny smell' when an oven first turns on is very common. If it's a new appliance, it's likely the protective manufacturing oils burning off for the first time; this smells like hot plastic but should fade after a few cycles with the door open. Alternatively, if food or grease has splashed onto the heating elements (especially in a grill or base element), that will produce a distinct burnt smell. Also, does the smell resemble burning plastic/electrical wiring, or more like burnt food?
more like hot plastic or electrical I think, and it seems to come from behind or underneath, not inside the oven. its an old one, about 12 years

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A hot plastic or electrical smell coming from behind or underneath an oven that is 12 years old is a significant warning sign. It suggests an internal electrical component—such as the wiring insulation on the heating elements, the terminal block where power enters the appliance, or the fan motor—is overheating and melting. Because this involves mains voltage and high heat, it presents a fire risk. Please do not attempt to open the rear panel yourself; leave the oven switched off and unplugged (or isolated at the fuse box) until a qualified engineer can inspect the internal wiring and connections.

plan: Safety: a burning smell was reported. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It stays switched off and unplugged. Give the owner checks that are safe with it unplugged and cool and could show the cause (fluff or lint, a blocked or crushed vent, a jammed belt or brush bar, a food spill), as clear steps. Say plainly that if the smell was electrical (hot plastic or wiring), there was smoke or there are scorch marks, or the checks find no simple cause, it must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. Never say or imply that it is safe to use again.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell when it's on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
